terms.comment: Classically a point or dot of any kind (Lewis & Short); its use for the sign that ends a sentence is modern. Traupman also gives pūnctum for any punctuation mark (248).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 248.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
